uutiset.t: Netflix Buys Seinfeld Studio Lot After Goldman Forecloses
uutiset.s: Bloomberg's John Gittelsohn joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Netflix announced it’s buying Radford Studio Center, the historic Los Angeles lot where Seinfeld was filmed, for $380 million after Goldman Sachs Group took control of the property. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Blue Owl, Blackstone Make Rare Pension Deal
uutiset.s: Bloomberg's Layan Odeh joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." A top US pension is considering raising roughly $4 billion in a complex financing bundling stakes in private credit funds managed by Blackstone, Blue Owl Capital and others, according to people familiar with the matter. (Source: Bloomber

uutiset.s: Bloomberg's Naomi Kresge joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." Sanofi shares climbed on Wednesday to the highest since May 2025, adding to yesterday’s strong gains following the announcement of its planned acquisition of US drugmaker Insmed. uutiset.t: Egypt Road Accident Kills at Least 30 in Greater Cairo
uutiset.s: At least 30 people were killed in Greater Cairo after a truck carrying petroleum products caught fire in one Egypt’s deadliest road accidents in years.

uutiset.t: GTCR Is Said to Weigh $50B Global Payments Buyout
uutiset.s: Bloomberg's Mengqi Sun joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." GTCR confirmed in a filing that it’s exploring a takeover of Global Payments in what would be one of the biggest-ever leveraged buyouts. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: BNP Paribas Hit by Higher Capital Surcharge Under New GSIB List
uutiset.s: BNP Paribas SA was hit with an extra 50 basis points capital requirement by the Financial Stability Board after the French bank moved into a different tier for the world’s most systemically important banks.

uutiset.t: Stocks Continue Fall as Nvidia Reinstatement Rally Fades
uutiset.s: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day than "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Nvidia U-Turn Is Bad News For Anthropic, Says Parmy Olson
uutiset.s: Bloomberg Opinion columnist Parmy Olson said that the tumult surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and subsequent reinstatement isn't good news for Anthropic given how the companies' ethos and leaders differ in relation to AI development and government ties. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.s: Tom Kloza, chief energy advisor to Gulf Oil, said that he expects a 'major head fake' from the oil market as the 'seeds' for the next oil rally have been planted and could take gas and diesel prices back up in the beginning of 2027. uutiset.t: M&A in the Industrials Sector Looks Set for a Robust 2027
uutiset.s: Industrial M&A activity is set to remain strong in 2027, driven by a clutch of rapidly growing sectors in the space.

uutiset.t: La Caisse’s Infrastructure Arm Pauses Bond Sale as Market Sours
uutiset.s: Deteriorating conditions in financial markets are preventing a new Canadian issuer from selling debt as planned, even with the backing of one of the country’s most important pension managers.

uutiset.t: Still Mispricing in Private Markets: Weinstein
uutiset.s: Adam Weinstein, president and & COO of New Mountain Capital, joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." They discuss the pricing of assets in private markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

Gayle Turk, partner at Centerview Partners, Brandon Van Dyke, M&A partner at Skadden, and Bloomberg's David Carnevali, join Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." They discuss that despite AI worries, market selloffs, and political change in DC, M&A will continue to thrive into 2027. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Lower Multiples Will Bring PE Back: Kindler
uutiset.s: Robert Kindler, global chair of the M&A group at Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison, joins Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Deals." They discussed the record pace for M&A and his outlook for 2027. (Source: Bloomberg)

uutiset.t: Michael Burry Is More Long Than Short After Dumping Nasdaq Puts
uutiset.s: The selloff in technology stocks has left investor Michael Burry, who became famous for betting against the US mortgage market in 2008, with more long equity positions than short ones after unloading his put options on the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index.
